summary.text: A 53-year-old man with decompensated alcohol-associated cirrhosis, ESRD and prior HE (before and after a TIPS placed five years earlier for refractory ascites, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and variceal bleeding) was listed for liver-kidney transplant (MELD 25) and was admitted after two days of severe nausea and non-bloody emesis. On admission he had right lower quadrant tenderness and normal mental function; ammonia was 40 µmol/L (normal), lactate 5.9 mmol/L, total bilirubin 4.6 mg/dL, INR 1.52, creatinine 6.3 mg/dL, and MELD-Na was 29.

Twelve hours after admission he became unresponsive to pain with a right gaze preference and right leg weakness. Head CT showed subtle loss of grey-white differentiation and CTA with perfusion was unremarkable. He developed acute hypoxic respiratory failure requiring intubation. Repeat labs (table column labelled 6 Hours; timing versus the narrative unresolved) showed ammonia 810 µmol/L, lactate 10.9 mmol/L and procalcitonin 89.4 ng/mL, and Doppler ultrasound showed a patent TIPS.

Six hours later he developed bilateral myoclonic jerks without epileptiform EEG activity, attributed to grade IV HE, and repeat head CT showed cerebral edema. He received deep sedation (propofol, midazolam; RASS goal -4 to -5), permissive hypocapnia, therapeutic hypothermia, hypertonic saline, mannitol and broad-spectrum antibiotics, plus lactulose, rifaximin, zinc sulfate, CVVHD and concurrent high-volume TPE over two days. The authors describe this as acute-onset severe hyperammonemia with fulminant intracranial hypertension in a patient with acute-on-chronic liver failure.

Ammonia fell from a maximum of 979 to 169 µmol/L but the neurological condition continued to deteriorate. Head CT 72 hours after admission showed worsening cerebral and cerebellar edema, new bilateral uncal and downward tonsillar/central herniation and pontine Duret microhemorrhages, and he was declared brain dead twelve hours later.

article_limitations: Table 1 repeat column is labelled "6 Hours" while the narrative places the decline at twelve hours and then reports repeat labs; literal header kept, no timing asserted.
Table creatinine and albumin and INR rows print no unit; creatinine unit mg/dL comes from the admission narrative only (6.3 mg/dL vs table 6.29). Heart-rate and blood-pressure units are not printed.
Text gives final ammonia 169 µmol/L whereas Figure 1 plots lower later points; Figure 1 therapy/event markers are plotted at hours not stated in text (visual submission only).

Background temperature (33-34 C), mannitol-bolus recommendations and ICP-monitoring suggestions in the discussion are literature statements, not patient-specific performed actions; RASS -4 to -5 is a sedation goal, not an achieved score. Concentrations, doses, and PaCO2/temperature targets for this patient are not reported.
Discussion statements cite published cohorts and trials; no explicit same-patient prior report is identified and none is attributed to the index patient.
